newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin back to work on Monday after op recovery.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin back to work on Monday after op recovery.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin will return to Moscow from his country residence at the weekend and will begin work in his Kremlin office on Monday, seven weeks after open heart surgery, his press secretary said on Friday.

Sergei Yastrzhembsky told a news briefing that the 65-year-old president was ready to resume work but added that doctors wanted him to maintain a gentle pace in order not to harm his recovery from the November 5 bypass operation.
"We will do our utmost to make his return a smooth process," he said.

Yastrzhembsky also recalled the prediction of pioneering U.S. heart surgeon Michael DeBakey, who advised on Yeltsin's operation, that the president had "at least 10 years of active working life" ahead on condition that he did not overdo things.
Interfax news agency quoted Yastrzhembsky as saying later that Yeltsin was planning to make his first televised address to the nation since the operation later on Friday.
"This is completely possible," a duty officer in the presidential press office told Reuters.
Yastrzhembsky said that Yeltsin's plans for his first days back at work included meetings with Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, Kremlin chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais and other senior officials.

But he denied media reports that Yeltsin, who has spent more than two weeks in the Rus residence some 100 km (65 miles) west of Moscow, intended to mark his return to work with dramatic personnel changes in his entourage.
Communist leader Gennady Zyuganov has demanded the sacking of Chubais as a price for his support of the draft 1997 budget in parliament.
"One should not expect that the president's return to work will immediately herald weighty decisions affecting the country's fate," Yastrzhembsky said.
The interview, recorded by the Kremlin press service, was recorded in the Rus residence outside Moscow where the 65-year-old Russian leader has spent the final stage of his post-operation recovery.
Yeltsin, dressed in a cardigan and open-neck shirt and sitting in an armchair, spoke decisively and firmly.

"I feel that the recovery period is over. I am returning to the Kremlin on Monday, (December) 23. I will be there at nine a.m. The doctors have done their job and now it is up to the president," he said.
Yeltsin said the main problems he would have to address upon his return were workers' unpaid wages, the peace process in the breakaway Chechnya region and reform of the army.
